title_protection.quote: Using the designation Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathy, physician, surgeon, physician and surgeon, Dr., M.D., or D.O., or a similar designation, or any combination thereof, in the conduct of an occupation or profession pertaining to the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of human disease or condition, unless the designation additionally contains the description of another branch of the healing arts for which one holds a valid license in the State.

scope_protection.quote: A person who practices or attempts to practice medicine contrary to the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a class F felony
scope_protection.citation: § 1766. Penalties [See conflicting amendment, unable to be implemented, in 75 Del. Laws, c. 161, § 5.]

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of false, fraudulent, or forged statements or documents in connection with certification, registration, or licensing requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use of any false, fraudulent, or forged statement or document or the use of any fraudulent, deceitful, dishonest, or unethical practice in connection with a certification, registration, or licensing requirement of this chapter
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conduct that would constitute a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conduct that would constitute a crime substantially related to the practice of medicine;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any dishonorable, unethical, or other conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practice of medicine under a false or assumed name
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter under a false or assumed name;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practice of medicine without a certificate or other authorizing document
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter without a certificate or other authorizing document or renewal of such document, unless otherwise authorized by this chapter;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use, distribution, or issuance of a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use, distribution, or issuance of a prescription for a dangerous or narcotic drug, other than for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising of the practice of medicine in an unethical or unprofessional manner
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising of the practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter in an unethical or unprofessional manner;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Solicitation or acceptance of a fee by fraudulent representation that an incurable condition can be permanently cured
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Solicitation or acceptance of a fee from a patient or other person by fraudulent representation that a manifestly incurable condition, as determined with reasonable medical certainty, can be permanently cured;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowing or intentional performance of an act that assists an unauthorized person to practice medicine
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowing or intentional performance of an act which, unless authorized by this chapter, assists an unauthorized person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under a certified physician
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The failure to provide adequate supervision to an individual working under the supervision of a person who is certified and registered to practice medicine;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Misconduct including sexual misconduct, incompetence, or gross negligence or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Misconduct, including but not limited to sexual misconduct, incompetence, or gross negligence or pattern of negligence in the practice of medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful violation of the confidential relationship with or confidential communications of a patient;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to report to the Board as required regarding treating an impaired physician
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by § 1730(a) of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to report hospital privilege actions or medical society disciplinary actions to the Board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by § 1730(b) of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to report malpractice claims to the Board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board as required by § 1730(c) of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unjustified failure to divulge information relevant to authorization or competence of another practitioner
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unjustified failure upon request to divulge information relevant to the authorization or competence of a person to practice medicine or other profession or occupation regulated under this chapter to the Board
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of a provision of this chapter or a board order or regulation likely to harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The violation of a provision of this chapter or the violation of an order or regulation of the Board related to medical procedures or to the procedures of other professions or occupations regulated under this chapter, the violation of which more probably than not will harm or injure the public or an individual;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional services rendered
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Charging a grossly exorbitant fee for professional or occupational services rendered;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suspension, revocation, or other disciplinary action by a regulatory authority in another state or territory
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Suspension or revocation of a certificate to practice medicine or of the authorizing document to practice another profession or occupation regulated under this chapter, or other disciplinary action taken by the regulatory authority in another state or territory.
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Signing the death certificate of a person prior to the actual time of death of the person;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of electronic prescription requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A violation of §1764A of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to report to the Board as required under § 1731A
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to report to the Board when required by §1731A of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful failure to comply with minor treatment/examination chaperone requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Wilful failure to comply with §1769B of this title;
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in conversion therapy with a child
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in conversion therapy with a child; and
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Referring a child to a provider in another jurisdiction to receive conversion therapy
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Referring a child to a provider in another jurisdiction to receive conversion therapy.
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice medicine with reasonable skill or safety due to mental or physical disability or serious health condition
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A certificate to practice medicine is subject to restriction, suspension, or revocation, either temporarily or permanently, in case of the inability of a physician to practice medicine with reasonable skill or safety to patients by reason of a mental or physical disability or serious health condition
disciplinary_grounds.citation: § 1731. Unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

establishment_regulation_required.quote: No person licensed under this chapter shall perform any office-based surgery, as defined in § 122(3)y. of Title 16, in a facility unless such facility is accredited or licensed in accordance with § 122(3)z. of Title 16.
establishment_regulation_required.citation: § 1705. Accreditation of facilities where office-based surgeries are performed.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of medicine" or "practice medicine" includes: a. Advertising, holding out to the public, or representing in any manner that one is authorized to practice medicine in this State; b. Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person; c. Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person, including the management of pregnancy and parturition; d. Offering or undertaking to perform a surgical operation upon another person; e. Rendering a written or otherwise documented medical opinion concerning the diagnosis or treatment of a person...; f. Rendering a determination of medical necessity or a decision affecting or modifying the diagnosis and/or treatment of a person; g. Using the designation Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathy, physician, surgeon...
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine" or "practice medicine" includes: a. methods_authorized.quote: Offering or undertaking to prevent or to diagnose, correct, and/or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, or devices a disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, defect, or abnormal physical or mental condition of another person, including the management of pregnancy and parturition; d. Offering or undertaking to perform a surgical operation upon another person;

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe drugs and medicine; electronic prescribing is required with specified exceptions. A violation of prescription requirements is unprofessional conduct.
drug_authority.quote: Offering or undertaking to prescribe, order, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another person;

license_status_types.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure, including payment of a fee set by the Division of Professional Regulation, except that an applicant for an administrative medicine license shall not be required to show that the applicant has been engaged in the active practice of medicine

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates from schools listed in IMED must pass the ECFMG examination and the Federation of State Medical Boards examination. Graduates from schools not listed in IMED must also complete 3 years of postgraduate training in an ACGME-approved residency program, plus pass the ECFMG and FSMB examinations. All clinical rotations in the US or Canada must have been conducted at institutions with formal affiliation with an AMA- or AOA-approved medical school or in hospitals with ACGME-approved residency programs.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A degree of Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathy, or an equivalent degree, from a legally incorporated medical college or school located in a country other than the United States or Canada, which medical college or school is not listed in the International Medical Education Directory (IMED), but the applicant has completed 3 years of postgraduate training in a residency program which has been approved by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education and has successfully passed the examination administered by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates and the Federation of State Medical Boards

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: "Collaborative agreement" means a written document expressing an arrangement of collaboration between a licensed physician and a physician assistant.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants have prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice, subject to biennial renewal. They cannot prescribe independently but require a collaborative agreement.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: Prescriptive authority for therapeutic drugs and treatments within the scope of physician assistant practice. The physician assistant's prescriptive authority and authority to practice as a physician assistant are subject to biennial renewal upon application to the Physician Assistant Regulatory Council

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: A collaborating physician may not at any given time collaborate with more than 4 physician assistants, unless a regulation of the Board increases or decreases the number.
max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.citation: § 1771. Physician's role in collaborating with a physician assistant.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued has a duty to report to the Board, within 60 days, all information concerning medical malpractice claims settled or adjudicated to final judgment
malpractice_reporting_required.citation: § 1730. Duty to report unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine is issued and health care facility as defined in § 1740 of this title has a duty to report to the Board within 30 days: a. Any partial or full removal of hospital privileges based on adverse events, unprofessional conduct or competency issues
hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.citation: § 1730. Duty to report unprofessional conduct and inability to practice medicine.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The Executive Director may defer the investigation of a report pending a reported licensee's evaluation and treatment for substance abuse or for physical or mental illness, provided sufficient safeguards exist to protect the licensee's patients and the public. Safeguards may include a verifiable, voluntary cessation of the practice of medicine or a limited or monitored practice.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the Executive Director reasonably believes that a diagnostic mental or physical examination of the person under investigation is necessary, the Executive Director shall order the person to submit to an examination at the person's expense to be conducted by a physician or agency designated by the Executive Director. Every person to whom a certificate to practice medicine has been issued is deemed to have given that person's own consent to submit to a diagnostic mental or physical examination when so directed by the Executive Director
compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.citation: § 1732. Investigations of complaints; Executive Director authority.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: The Board may issue an administrative medicine license to a physician who meets all qualifications for licensure, including payment of a fee set by the Division of Professional Regulation, except that an applicant for an administrative medicine license shall not be required to show that the applicant has been engaged in the active practice of medicine, as defined in the Board's regulations. Administrative medicine licensees may not provide medical or clinical services to or for patients

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: The applicant for whom the examination is to be waived is licensed, certified, registered, or otherwise legally qualified to practice medicine in another state of the United States or in another jurisdiction, and seeks a temporary certificate to practice medicine for not less than 2 weeks nor more than 3 months for the purpose of taking charge of the practice of a person certified and registered to practice medicine in this State during the person's temporary illness or absence from this State.
locum_tenens_permit_available.citation: § 1722. Waiver of professional examination for temporary certification, for hospital or institution staff, for physicians licensed in another jurisdiction, and for physicians passing an alternative exam.
